ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC SDN List, OFAC Non-SDN Consolidated List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) sanctions designations, and Korean government restrictions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For every UBO, senior manager, director, officer, authorized signatory, and high-risk counterparty, run real-time AML/KYC verification, PEP identification via government and commercial databases, negative-news screening, and continuous monitoring. Enhanced due diligence applies if a shareholder controls more than 25%, if any payment rail involves third-party Stripe or SWIFT intermediaries, or if anti-cheat middleware is supplied to foreign gaming operators with potential sanctions nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (www.iros.go.kr) - Company Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in the Korean alphabet (Hangeul). Latin-script names are accepted only if transliterated phonetically into Hangeul and must appear as a legally distinguishable trade name. The statutory four-tier naming sequence is: distinctive word, business category identifier, industry descriptor, and legal-form suffix. For a limited liability company, the suffix must be Yuhan Hoesa. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to a previously registered domestic company's trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under the Commercial Registration Act, upon rejection the registry issues a written ground. The applicant must file an appeal with the head of the competent district court registry within 14 days of notification, setting out the exact statutory basis and supporting evidence, including the rejected name, a proposed corrected name, and a notarized copy of the applicant's authorization. The court registrar will decide within 21 days; if refused, the applicant may file a fresh reservation without referencing the original name and may apply to the district court for a formal adjudication under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. No oral hearing is ordinarily held.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk software company, a registered virtual office or commercial mailbox is technically permissible for Korean incorporation provided there is a written lease agreement and a designated service contact. However, the National Tax Service and financial institutions strongly disfavor pure virtual offices for this industry because they impede issuance of electronic tax invoices for exported services, obstruct bank beneficial-owner verification, and may prevent zero-rated VAT refund claims for cross-border gaming middleware. A shared executive office with physical reception and meeting space is compliant; a mailbox-only address is rejected by most Korean banks for corporate account opening and by the National Tax Service for substance checks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: a) absence of any employee or director at the registered office during business hours; b) no nameplate or lease documentation at the address; c) no physical equipment, server, or records; d) the same address is used by multiple unrelated corporate shells; e) annual revenue is inconsistent with declared headcount; f) unannounced tax office visit is triggered by abnormal e-Tax invoice patterns. Quantified risk: a low baseline of 6% per taxing year for a compliant shared executive office, rising to 35% for a pure mailbox-only arrangement or if tax filing red flags are generated. A physically attended address with at least one local director or employee is the recommended buffer.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended by Act No. 17758, December 29, 2020), Articles 288, 289, 290, 291, 292, 295, 313, 317, 318, 331, 332, 388, 393, 399, 400, 542-2 and 543-1; Korean Inheritance and Gift Tax Act Article 8 for fully paid quota capital; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 17836) for any non-resident equity participation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office, Commercial Registration Division, Supreme Court of Korea (via Korean Court E-filing System / 인터넷등기소)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (법인설립등기신청서) accompanied by the Notarized Articles of Incorporation (정관) and the Corporate Registration Clearance Certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Korean Commercial Act after the 2012 amendment. The only capital requirement is that the full amount of each quota (지분) as stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be paid in cash into the company's temporarily established depository bank account before or at the time of incorporation registration. The bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit, which is filed with the registry. There is no governmental blocked escrow account requirement beyond this ordinary deposit; capital becomes immediately usable after registration, subject to the Capital Regulation Rules of the Commercial Act prohibiting payment-in-kind unless certain statutory asset valuation reports are obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA. RESOLVED, that the first meeting of the Board of Directors (the 'Board') of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company') is hereby duly convened and held on this [●] day of [●], [●], at the principal office of the Company located at [●-gu, [●]-si, Republic of Korea], with each director being present either in person or via electronic communication in accordance with Article [●] of the Articles of Incorporation and Article 393 of the Commercial Act. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. RESOLVED, that the Board acknowledges and confirms that all quota capital subscriptions have been fully and irrevocably subscribed in cash by the incorporators in accordance with the quota subscription schedule set forth in the supplementary subscription ledger, and that each subscriber has paid the full amount of his or her subscribed quota into the Company's temporary depository bank account maintained with [Bank Name, Branch, Account Number] as evidenced by the certificate of capital deposit and the account ledger produced to the Board. The Board hereby adopts said payment schedule, directs the corporate secretary to transmit the certificate of capital deposit with the incorporation application, and approves the allocation of quotas as reflected in the ledger. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Board designates the following bank accounts as the primary cash management and operational accounts of the Company: [Account Titles, Bank, SWIFT Code, Currency] and authorizes the Representative Director acting together with the Chief Financial Officer (jointly and severally) to open, operate, close, and maintain deposit accounts, sign all checks, initiate and approve electronic funds transfers through SWIFT Wire and all other payment rail mechanisms, and issue all associated account documentation. The Board further mandates that any single transfer exceeding KRW 100,000,000 or any aggregate transfer exceeding KRW 300,000,000 in one calendar month shall require a prior written board authorization and dual signature control. 3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is hereby adopted as the address stated in Article 2 of the Articles of Incorporation, and the Representative Director is directed to promptly cause the company to register such address with the Local District Court Registry Office and to notify the National Tax Service and any other relevant authority of any relocation within 14 days of adoption. The Board further authorizes the Representative Director to execute and deliver the office lease agreement in the Company's name and to maintain all statutory records, vouchers, and minute books at the registered office. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Representative Director (대표이사), [Name] be and is hereby appointed Director, and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Auditor, each to hold office until the end of the first annual general meeting of members following incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each officer shall have the authority and responsibility assigned by the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation, and the Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver all statutory forms, regulatory filings, banking documents, and employment agreements as may be necessary to carry out the business of the Company, specifically including the development and licensing of anti-cheat engine middleware. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board delegates to the Representative Director the authority to file the Company's application for business registration with the Korean National Tax Service, to enroll the Company with the National Pension, National Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance programs, and to apply for any patents, utility models, software copyright registrations, or other intellectual property protection for the Company's anti-cheat algorithms and kernel-level integrity middleware. THIS RESOLUTION is effective immediately upon execution and shall be signed by all current directors as witness to the unanimous consent granted herein. Each director certifies that this resolution conforms to the Articles of Incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act, and the resolution may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean-accredited Notary Public (notary office in jurisdiction of registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation for Yuhan Hoesa including the exact corporate name in Korean and English, the purpose clause describing kernel-level anti-cheat middleware development, software publishing, and consultation services, the address of the registered office, the total quota capital, number of quotas, and the allocation among incorporators. Execute the articles before a Korean notary public; the notary will verify the identity and legal capacity of each incorporator. After notarization, open a temporary depository bank account under the Company's name with a commercial bank and deposit the full subscription amount. Obtain the bank certificate of capital deposit and the subscription ledger. Also prepare the corporate seal registration documents if the company plans to use a corporate seal; notarization of the seal exemplification is required for later banking and registration filings. All documents must be in Korean; if any director is non-resident or foreign, provide apostilled passports and Korean consular-legalized powers of attorney as needed.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
Quota subscription ledger with full signatures
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Temporary depository bank account registration confirmation
Lease agreement for the registered office
Passports/ID and resident registration copies of all incorporators
Foreign investor notification certificate (if any foreign shareholder)
Power of attorney (if executed by proxy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a correction request, the incorporators must amend the articles and re-execute before the same notary, which will reset the SLA clock to 3 business days. If the depository bank refuses the temporary account due to name conflict or resident status issues, either (i) open the account in the name of one incorporator that is identical to the company name pre-registration, or (ii) use a local certified public accountant or legal representative with a power of attorney; the certificate can be re-issued on the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Commercial Registration Division, Supreme Court of Korea e-filing portal internetso.slr.scourt.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for incorporation registration of the Yuhan Hoesa through the court e-filing system or by paper filing at the district court registry office with jurisdiction over the registered office address. The Commercial Act requires the registration within 20 days from signing the articles; the application must contain the company name, purpose, registered office, total capital, director and auditor names, and the authorised representative. Attach the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, and written consents of each statutory officer. Pay the court registration fee based on the capital amount (approximately KRW 140,000 for registered capital below 100 million KRW, but may exceed if capital is higher); the official fee printed on the registration receipt is required for subsequent tax filings. The registry will check for compliance with public policy, corporate capacity, and statutory documents; upon approval, the court issues the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인등기사항증명서), which is the conclusive evidence of the company's legal personality and the starting point of business existence.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit
Consent to appointment of each director and auditor
Certificate of identity and resident registration of each officer
Power of attorney (if filed by a professional representative)
Court fee payment receipt
Corporate seal registration certificate
Foreign investor reporting confirmation from Ministry of Economy and Finance (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registry issues a supplementary document request, the applicant generally receives 14 calendar days to cure; file the missing documents electronically with a cover declaration. If the court suspends registration, a written explanation of the legal grounds must be submitted; if the suspension continues beyond 10 business days, the applicant may file a formal peremptory application to the registry director, and later a complaint to the High Court through the Trial of Registration Procedures under Article 214 of the Registration of Real Estate Act, but in practice a pre-filing consultation at the registry window resolves most issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and VAT Enrollment with National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (e.g., Jung-gu Tax Office) under the National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax – 이택스 portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 calendar days after the end of the month during which the incorporation registration is effective, file Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) with the NTS local tax office. The application requests a Business Registration Number and a corporate tax ID for VAT and withholding. Register as a value-added tax payer (general or simplified, though Yuhan Hoesa is generally a general corporate VAT taxpayer). Also apply for the e-tax invoice issuance certificate and, if the company anticipates payroll, register for employee withholding. The tax office will review the company's registered address and verify the lease agreement and certificate of incorporation. After obtaining the business registration certificate, the company must register its bank account and corporate seal with the NTS for electronic tax invoices.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration certificate (법인등기사항증명서)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation copy
Business registration application form (NTS-3071)
Registered office lease agreement (original)
Representative director's ID and resident registration copy
Corporate seal certificate
Bank account certificate and account number
Information on business activity codes (ISIC 6201) and subsidiary codes for software development and gaming middleware
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS issues a notice of supplemental information, respond within 14 days; if the business registration is blocked by a mismatch between the registered address and the actual office, provide a revised lease contract and corporate resolution showing that the office is the same as the registered address. For tax office processing delays, one can contact the taxpayer services division via HomeTax live chat and request expedited issuance; if the certificate is not issued after 7 business days, file a complaint with the Taxpayer Rights Examiner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Pension Service (NPS), National Health Insurance Service (NHIS), Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service (KWCWS), and local employment security office (Ministry of Employment and Labor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days of hiring employees, and immediately for directors who are also employees, register the company as a workplace under the following four social insurance systems: National Pension, National Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance. File the 'Acquisition of Workplace Registration' application with the respective online portals (4insure.or.kr) and the Ministry of Employment and Labor. Submit the employment rules and company's labor contract templates, and if the company has 50 or more employees, adopt an autonomous workplace safety and health management plan under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. For a software development office, workspace fire-safety inspection certificates are required before issuance of the employment insurance certificate. The platform authentication uses the business registration number and the corporate seal certificate.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate copy
Incorporation registration certificate
Certificate of corporate seal
Director appointment resolutions
Employment contract template and actual contracts for each hired employee
List of overseas employee data handling (if any PIPA filing needed)
Corporate lease agreement
Representative director's resident registration copy
Workplace fire-safety inspection approval (standard office)
Workplace setup form for each social insurance scheme
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social insurance registration is rejected because the business registration number cannot be verified, synchronize the NTS business certificate with the insurance portals by re-entering and submitting a claim; if the issue is an incomplete workplace address, update the business registration certificate with NTS and re-file. If the insurance application is delayed, raise a query on the 4insure.or.kr and request a manual confirmation, with a maximum SLA of 10 additional days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Seoul (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank) and the Financial Supervisory Service for anti-money laundering compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current account and foreign currency account using the incorporation registration certificate and corporate seal certificate. The bank will perform a transaction pattern interview with the representative director or a designated manager for AML/CTF purposes, and will require board resolution authorizing signatories. Present the complete company suite of documents, and verify that the business registration certificate lists the exact physical office address. After the account is opened, request a bank letter confirming the SWIFT/BIC code and correspondent banking details for inbound Wire transfers. For Stripe settlement, configure the payout bank account in the Stripe dashboard; Stripe will require the company tax ID and the corporate resolution for payout signatory. Additionally, if the company will process personal data of game users in the EEA or Korea, appoint a privacy manager and register with the PIPA as needed, though this is not part of bank account licensing.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration certificate
Business registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Original seal and representative director's identification card
Board resolution authorizing bank signatories and payment rails
Passport / resident registration of the authorized signatory
Latest corporate minutes and certificate of officers
Lease agreement to verify physical office
Proof of capital payment if a bank inspection requires it
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for an in-person verification of the representative director, schedule a branch meeting within 7 days. If the bank flags potential money laundering due to a high-risk jurisdiction payment rail, provide a detailed cash flow plan and opinion letter from the company's Korean legal counsel; if the bank still refuses, apply to an alternative commercial bank and file a no-reason explanation complaint with the Financial Supervisory Service if there is no documented compliance basis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – none; the enterprise is a pure digital software development company (ISIC 6201, NAICS 541511) operating from an ordinary office. No industrial manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing facilities are involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – the development and licensing of kernel-level anti-cheat middleware does not constitute game publishing or distribution in the Republic of Korea, and does not trigger a mandatory governmental license under the Game Industry Promotion Act. The only administrative prerequisite is a valid business registration certificate, a standard corporate tax ID, and adherence to data protection law. If the company later expands to game hosting or publishing services, prior GRAC content rating and the 'Application for Confirmation of Distribution' under Article 12(3) of that Act would become mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – Ministry of Environment and Korea Environmental Corporation have no jurisdiction over software development activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – the project is an office-based digital service activity, which is expressly exempt from the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (Act No. 17204) because it involves no physical construction, discharge, or land modification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – the facility emits no point-source wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous air pollutants, or EHS discharges. Standard waste electrical and electronic equipment recycling duties under the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources apply only to hardware disposed of in the office, and the company should use certified e-waste handlers; no emission thresholds exist for pure software development.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – the company will lease a general office. The Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters or the local fire safety authority will require a standard Fire Safety Certificate for the leased office (fire extinguishers, exit signage, sprinkler inspection) pursuant to the Fire Services Act; this is a condition of the lease and a prerequisite for the business registration certificate renewal, but not a separate 'industrial license.' Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the company must submit an 'Industrial Safety and Health Management Standard' to the regional office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor if it employs over 50 persons, and must provide standardized ergonomics and anti-eye-fatigue procedures for computer workstations. No special civil defense clearance, structural load examination, or hazardous materials permit is required.

stage_2.compliance_notes: This company does not require an industrial operating license; the anti-cheat engine middleware is purely digital, and the EIA tier is 'Not Applicable' as stated above. All banking and tax permits are administrative not industrial.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS) is the competent authority for customs and export/import declarations; online electronic portal: UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the entity maintains a domestic place of business in Korea. If the foreign-owned KR_YUHANGHOESA operates through a Korean Yuhan Hoesa or a domestic business establishment, registration is mandatory before business commencement. Step 2: File the Business Registration Application with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered Korean business address, either in person or through the resident director, statutory representative, or duly appointed tax representative. Step 3: Submit the certificate of incorporation or foreign equivalent, articles of incorporation or memorandum, power of attorney, evidence of the Korean place of business, identity/alien registration documents of the representative, and a statement of expected taxable activities. Step 4: Upon approval, obtain the Business Registration Certificate carrying the 10-digit Korean tax identification number, which functions as both the Corporate Taxpayer ID and the VAT registration number. Step 5: For physical export/import activities, also register with Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS to obtain the Korean importer/exporter code linked to the NTS tax identification number. Step 6: If the foreign non-resident entity has no domestic place of business but is electively registered for VAT, the NTS may require appointment of a domestic tax representative and, in appropriate cases, a security or bond under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is treated as a per se corporation under the Korean Commercial Act and is taxed under the Corporation Tax Act at entity level on its worldwide income subject to foreign tax credit relief. Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box pass-through election for domestic limited liability companies. Hybrid mismatch adjustments under the International Tax Adjustment Act, controlled foreign company rules, and thin capitalization rules may apply to cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary VAT registration threshold applies in Korea. Any business person with a domestic business establishment must apply for VAT registration before making taxable supplies. A simplified taxable person regime exists for businesses with annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000, but registration itself remains mandatory; this turnover threshold affects VAT calculation and reporting only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT taxpayers in Korea, including foreign-owned domestic entities, must issue electronic tax invoices through National Tax Service HomeTax or through an NTS-certified electronic tax invoice issuance service provider. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS by the statutory deadline, ordinarily on the day following the invoice issue date or within the aggregation period permitted under the Value-Added Tax Act. The NTS receives e-tax invoice data through secure API, EDI, and web-service channels in HomeTax and cross-matches such data with VAT returns, corporate tax filings, foreign exchange settlement records, and Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations. Korea does not operate a Latin American style real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory anti-fraud digital stamping system, but the NTS applies automated matching, risk scoring, and audit selection to detect false invoices and mismatched export zero-rating claims. Taxpayers may use the NTS public API or certified commercial issuance platforms and must retain the original electronic records for the statutory retention period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, 0% VAT applies to goods that are physically exported from Korea and cleared by Korea Customs Service under an export declaration. For services, 0% VAT applies to supplies made from a Korean place of business to a non-resident or foreign enterprise where the consideration is received in foreign currency and the service is not consumed in Korea; this includes qualifying export of gaming anti-cheat middleware, software licenses, updates, and integrity service subscriptions supplied under a cross-border contract to an overseas game developer. The Korean entity must substantiate that the recipient is a non-resident, the payment is received in convertible foreign currency, the contractual risk and benefit sit outside Korea, and the digital service is actually delivered to and used overseas. If the service is deemed consumed in Korea or connected to the foreign entity's Korean business establishment, standard 10% VAT applies instead.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration submitted and cleared through UNI-PASS, evidencing physical movement of goods out of Korea; for electronically delivered anti-cheat engine services, the retained file must contain the system export service evidence because no customs entry is issued.
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing removal of exported goods from Korea to the overseas destination.

Commercial invoice and export sales contract identifying the non-resident purchaser, the ISIC 6201 anti-cheat middleware license, service period, quantity, unit prices, and stated consideration in foreign currency.

Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, functionally equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), showing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency in the Korean entity's foreign exchange account.

Zero-rated VAT electronic tax invoice and electronic service delivery or license usage logs demonstrating that the gaming security middleware was effectively delivered and consumed outside Korean territory.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Korea Customs Service performs post-clearance export audits while the NTS conducts VAT audits by matching electronic tax invoices, UNI-PASS export declarations, corporate income records, and foreign exchange settlement data. If export proceeds are not repatriated within the required foreign exchange settlement period or the zero-rating documentation is missing, contradictory, or forged, the NTS will reclassify the supply as domestic taxable, reverse any input VAT deducted or refunded, and re-assess VAT at the standard 10% headline rate on the export value. Additional tax and unjustified refund penalties are imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes; where the KCS export declaration or tax invoice is deliberately falsified, the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and Customs Act penalties apply, including criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and publication of the tax offense. Exporters should also expect clawback of refunded VAT together with interest and surcharges if the supporting customs and foreign exchange documents are not retained for the statutory audit period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a formally liberalised but supervisory-driven FX regime. Current-account transactions are fully convertible and do not require individual central bank permission; payments for software licensing, middleware subscriptions, royalties and cross-border business services qualify as current-account invisibles and may be remitted freely subject to Supporting Document Rules. Capital-account transactions, however, are subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act's quarantine principle: inbound equity injections, loans, acquisitions of foreign securities, and foreign-currency borrowings must be filed with a designated foreign exchange bank or, in large or exceptional cases, reported to the Bank of Korea or MOEF. The won's onshore exchange rate is market-determined in the Seoul Foreign Exchange Market, but the Korean Financial Supervisory Service and BOK impose macroprudential levies on short-term external debt and may exercise moral suasion during episodic volatility. For a Korean LLC owned by non-residents, profit remittance and liquidation proceeds are treated as current-account outbound transfers if backed by audited financial statements and tax payment certificates; however, any dividend distribution exceeding the bank's ordinary de minimis threshold triggers enhanced beneficiary-title verification. There is no forced surrender of export proceeds, but all foreign-currency receipts must be received through a designated foreign exchange bank account and supported by a customs or service export with an assigned transaction classification code. Repatriation of capital and exit proceeds may be blocked temporally if the outflow involves unresolved tax clearance, undisclosed bearer instruments, or mismatches between the capital contribution records and the Foreign Currency Acquisition Certificate. In practice, stringent identification of the ultimate economic beneficiary is the dominant friction, not exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds arising from goods or services must be collected within one year from the export declaration date or the service-rendering date, unless an extension is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank. No mandatory conversion ratio applies: the Korean regime permits 100% foreign-currency retention in an onshore foreign-currency account, so the LLC may hold KRW or USD at its discretion. The exporter must submit a received-export-proceeds report to the designated bank within 10 business days of deposit when the proceeds are not in the precise invoiced currency or when certain high-risk settlement patterns are triggered, and the bank is obliged to transmit data to the Bank of Korea for surveillance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational KRW/USD Dual Account
Corporate Current Account with Trade Services and FX Hedging Envelope
Foreign Investor Business Account (KRW) with Sub-Ledger USD Clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking infrastructure. South Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act require any entity holding customer funds or executing cross-border payments to hold a domestic banking licence or a licensed e-money/prepaid issuer licence from the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Offshore digital EMI operators such as Airwallex, Wise Business, Revolut Business or Payoneer are not recognised as designated foreign exchange banks and cannot issue Korean IBFs, KRW settlement accounts, or foreign-currency accounts for a Korean-domiciled legal entity. They may only be used as a complementary collection rail from overseas customers, but any KRW settlement into the Korean entity's tax registration must flow through a Tier-1 onshore bank. Attempting to route export revenues through an unlicensed EMI would create a foreign-currency acquisition violation, a VAT filing mismatch, and a criminal exposure under foreign exchange regulation. Therefore, treasury operations must be anchored in a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank with branch-level foreign exchange dealing capabilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned Korean LLC, physical presence is generally mandatory for the initial corporate account opening. Type-1 authorised signatories, the statutory director (even if a nominee must be disclosed), and the ultimate beneficial owner must appear in person at the bank branch to complete the Commercial Real-Time Transfer System and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act identity verification. Remote or consular-proxy opening is not permitted for foreign-owned Korean companies in the absence of a pre-existing private banking relationship, and even then, the FSC test bans fully remote acceptance. The bank will also require the company seal certificate (the official Seal of Incorporation), the foreign director's overseas proof of identification, a sworn Power of Attorney for the local authorised officer, and a notarised corporate resolution. Video-call verification may supplement, but never replace, the physical branch visit of the principal signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership concentration with a sole foreign shareholder above 75% and no local operations except one nominee director. Banks flag shell-company signature risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Korean Articles of Incorporation with stated business purpose matching ISIC 6201; signed and notarised shareholder register; substantive business plan detailing the anti-cheat middleware product, target customers, and engineering resources; proof of business premises in Korea (lease agreement or flexible office licence); monthly payroll or local service contracts for at least one Korean resident contractor; and audited or management accounts proving the company is not dormant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty or licensing income from the anti-cheat engine routed through zero-tax jurisdictions or intra-group invoicing structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete master-file and local-file documentation; arms-length transfer pricing policy for the middleware licensing fee; a fully-signed software licensing agreement with the overseas gaming publisher; invoices and settlement sheets matching the trade purpose code 9999-1-301 (computer software industrial property) or related IT service code; evidence that the code is actually hosted or served from Korean servers or by Korean engineers; and a beneficial ownership affidavit providing a through-chain ownership map to a natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound wire transfers from numerous global gaming publishers with inconsistent remitter names, potentially perceived as money mule settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A contractual counterparty register with legal entity identifiers (LEI or registration numbers) for all customers; a treasury policy restricting inbound payments to SWIFT MT103 from pre-approved bank accounts; sample invoices tied to each wire; a payment-reconciliation log reconciled to the anti-cheat licence activation logs or API usage metrics; and a data-use agreement proving the product is delivered digitally to known firms rather than to anonymous wallet intermediaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Software anti-cheat with kernel-level access may be considered a dual-use cyber-surveillance or malware-adjacent technology by a compliance committee, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A technical whitepaper and penetration-test report proving the product is not a malicious kernel driver; a legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming the anti-cheat tool does not violate the Korean Information and Communications Network Act or the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilisation; certification of compliance with the Game Industry Promotion Act (Article 12) and Personal Information Protection Act; and an acceptable-use policy expressly prohibiting use outside legitimate gaming anti-cheat enforcement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Korean LLC must be wired from a foreign corporate or individual account to the bank-designated Foreign Currency Acquisition Certificate account, using the SWIFT MT103 with repayment/reinvestment purpose code 1201-ER or 1202-ER under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remitter must be the foreign corporate's own account in a name matching the shareholder register; third-party payments are prohibited. After receipt, the bank issues a Foreign Currency Acquisition Certificate, which must be filed with KOTRA through the designated bank to complete foreign-investment registration. The funds are then converted to KRW at the market rate and made available for operating expenses only after the capital-verification statement is signed by the Korean external auditor. For amounts above KRW 100 million equivalent, the inbound remittance triggers a BOK surveillance report; for amounts above KRW 1 billion, a prior notification to MOEF's Foreign Exchange Policy Division may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound payments for settlement of trade payables, software royalties, subcontracting fees, and dealer commissions must be cleared through the designated bank's corporate internet-banking channel using SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers. For low-value recurring licensing or cloud-hosting invoices, the bank may authorise batch MT103 processing with static purpose codes. For purchase of third-party gaming engine licences or cybersecurity components, issuance of Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit is permissible but rarely necessary for intangible services; more efficient is a direct SWIFT transfer with supporting service agreement and invoice. Collections should be executed via Documentary Collections (DA/DP) only when dealing with a high-risk counterparty in a sanctions-sensitive territory; otherwise open-account MT103 netting is common. All outbound settlements above USD 50,000 require submission of the underlying contract and invoice to the bank's Foreign Exchange Information System; payments to sanctioned countries are blocked.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with a designated foreign exchange bank up to 12 months tenor, permitted only against underlying real trade/licensing exposures and evidenced by invoice forecasts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to offshore markets only; Korean residents and domestic branches may execute NDFs with BOK approval but as a corporate treasury the preferred instrument is the onshore deliverable forward
Currency swaps with maturities beyond 12 months require MOEF notification; plain KRW/USD plain-vanilla swaps are available from Tier-1 banks for cross-currency debt restructuring

Zero-cost collars and knock-in/knock-out options are permissible if transacted with a licensed Korean securities dealer or bank under the Capital Market Act, but options with speculative or over-hedged characteristics are prohibited by prudential guidelines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return with audited/unaudited financial statements, tax adjustment schedules and reporting statement (NTS corporate tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa: file by 31 March of the following year. Non-calendar fiscal year: within 3 months after fiscal year end. An audit-target entity may receive a one-month extension to 30 April for calendar-year filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing/untruthful return: 20% of unpaid corporation tax as a surcharge (40% when fraudulently suppressed). Omitted income and tax evasion charges may add up to 100% of unpaid tax. Late-payment surcharge: 0.025% per day of unpaid tax from the original due date. Persistent delinquency can trigger demand, seizure, revocation of business registration and judicial deregistration of a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return (local income tax final return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax office of the competent Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, Si/Gun or Gu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year end; standard calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa must file by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Similar unfaithful-return surcharge of 20% (40% for intentional concealment) plus per-day 0.025% late-payment surcharge. The local government may seize assets and enforce electronic tax collection through the national system if unpaid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA Audit Report and audited financial statements under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, submitted to financial regulator and to the annual members meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For statutory-audit targets, the audit must be completed before the annual members meeting which must be held by 31 March for calendar-year entities; the audit report must be submitted to FSS no later than 3 months after fiscal year end, and no later than 2 weeks after the auditor has delivered its report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint/submit: FSS can designate an auditor and impose administrative corrective orders; criminal and negligence fines under the External Audit Act apply, with fines up to KRW 30 million for certain reporting violations and public inspection/release of the violation. No automatic strike-off, but prolonged failure is an indicator of falsified books and can lead to tax fraud investigations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer withholding and payment statements for wage and retirement income (year-end settlement report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 10 March of the following taxable year for wage income payment records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit: 20% unfaithful-reporting surcharge plus per-day late-payment surcharge on any underwithheld tax; false payment statements can expose employer to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Report (foreign ownership, capital changes, business performance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year end; standard calendar-year foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa files by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million for failure to file or false filing; noncompliance may cancel foreign-investment tax and tariff benefits and affect foreign exchange bank reports.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit if, at the end of the preceding fiscal year: (1) total assets are at least KRW 12 billion; or (2) total assets are at least KRW 3 billion and annual revenue is at least KRW 20 billion; or (3) it is a parent/affiliate satisfying consolidated audit scope (with no headcount trigger under Korean law; headcount is not a statutory audit threshold for a Korean private LLC).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to the audit-required consolidated or separate financial statements of large/listed group entities; non-listed private Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as prescribed by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. Audit reports must state conformity with either K-IFRS or K-GAAP and figures are presented in Korean won.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a standalone annual beneficial-ownership filing for every Yuhan Hoesa. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any transfer or change in shares/ownership of a foreign-invested company must be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of the change. Under the Act on Reporting and Review of Specific Financial Information, a reporting entity must identify and verify the beneficial owner before a transaction and maintain records; a periodic annual confirmation may be produced internally and passed to the auditor. The member register must be updated without undue delay upon any share transfer, and the audited financial statements must list shareholders/members with holdings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,800 per annum for a Seoul or regional registered office/agent package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 - USD 45,000 per annum depending on asset size, transaction volume and K-IFRS vs K-GAAP complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national statutory corporate income tax rate (26.4% aggregate when the 10% local income tax surtax is included); lower progressive brackets: 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% over 200 million up to 20 billion, 22% over 20 billion up to 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box regime; available incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act include R&D tax credits, facility investment credits, employment-creation credits, and inward foreign-investment tax breaks under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, including a potential 3-year 100% corporate tax exemption and 50% reduction for the following 2 years in Free Economic Zones for qualifying high-technology gaming security middleware businesses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return (Corporate Tax Return) submitted through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing portal at hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the last day of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate identity, fiscal year, legal form (Yuhan Hoesa), ISIC code 6201 / NAICS 541511 for gaming anti-cheat middleware.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders or a foreign parent, disclose the foreign control relationship and enter the domestic withholding agent or permanent establishment (PE) details. Claim PE status only when core activities such as server operations, technical support, and developer supervision actually take place in Korea; otherwise classify income as limited Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total annual gross sales from software licensing, maintenance, gaming middleware subscriptions, and related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source revenue derived from anti-cheat engine licensing and technical services under Corporate Tax Act Article 119. Apply arm's length pricing for any cross-border transactions; reconcile Box 2 with the transfer pricing country-by-country and local file disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, tax-exempt income, and allowed deductions reducing gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may claim treaty-based reductions or exemptions only after the prescribed DTA relief application and submission of a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership proof. Unsupported treaty claims must not be deducted and anti-cheat source code sales are generally treated as royalty income subject to gross-basis withholding if no PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income reconciled to corporate taxable income through book-tax adjustments, including nondeductible expenses and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Perform PE profit attribution on a net basis when a Korean business is carried on; if a PE exists, controlled-transaction pricing, R&D cost contributions, and middleware server cost allocations must be documented under the International Tax Adjustment Act. Loss carryforward is available for ten years for current-fiscal-year losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate tax rates, local surtax, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited taxpayers without a Korean PE are subject only to final withholding on Korean-source dividends, interest, and royalties; no filing is required if the withholding agent has fully withheld. If a PE exists, file on net basis and use ordinary progressive rates plus the 10% local income tax surtax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Special Credits and Foreign Tax Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, tax treaty credits, and special tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident limited taxpayers, credit mechanisms are not applicable; DTA benefits should be claimed at source through the withholding agent. For resident corporate shareholder analysis, retained profits distributed to foreign investors will be subject to dividend withholding at the moment of distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the corporate tax return by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax of 20% of the underpaid national tax, plus statutory daily interest (approximately 0.022% per day) until paid. A deliberately false or fraudulent return may trigger an additional 40% penalty for unfaithful filing, and if evasion exceeds defined material thresholds criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to two years, liable to more than two years for aggravated cases) may be imposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% combined statutory withholding on outbound dividends to non-residents (20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax withholding); reduced to lower rates under Korea's bilateral income tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean withholding agent must apply the treaty rate only after the non-resident recipient submits (i) a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty country, (ii) a beneficial ownership and tie-breaker declaration confirming no abusive arrangement, and (iii) the prescribed NTS treaty relief application form. The documentation must be filed with the tax office together with the withholding return; if the application is not perfected before remittance, the 22% statutory rate is withheld and a refund must be sought through a formal NTS amended return within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis withholding on outbound interest and royalty payments to non-residents is 22% combined (20% national plus 2% local). Under typical Korean bilateral income tax treaties the rates are generally reduced to 10-15% for royalties and 5-15% for interest, and some treaties provide 0% dividend WHT for qualified shareholders participating at more than 10-25% in paid-up capital, subject to limitation-on-benefits provisions and Korean GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 (five billion won) aggregate annual international related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and, in certain cases, Master File preparation; separate notification of transactions is required in all cases.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not operate a rules-based Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime analogous to UAE or Bahrain; however, Korean tax authorities apply the general anti-abuse rule in the Framework Act for National Taxes, the beneficial ownership test under bilateral tax treaties, and OECD BEPS Action 6 standards to deny treaty benefits where a Yuhan Hoesa LLC lacks real economic activity. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) such as kernel-driver research, anti-cheat software code development, server monitoring, and licensing management must be performed in Korea for profits to be recognized there and for treaty claims to have substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Korean-source licensing revenue from the anti-cheat engine, fabrication of revenue records, or submission of false financial statements to the NTS to understate taxable income and avoid corporate income tax and transfer pricing adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; imprisonment for up to 2 years or a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded, in addition to the 40% unfaithful-return civil penalty and statutory daily interest on all unpaid national and local corporate income taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or knowingly permit fraudulent evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax through piercing of the corporate veil, may have personal bank and real estate assets seized by the NTS, may suffer a travel ban and tax-delinquent blacklisting, and may receive a criminal prison sentence of up to two years or more for aggravated evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, maintain, or submit the required Local File and Master File after exceeding the KRW 5 billion cross-border related-party transaction threshold, or pricing anti-cheat middleware royalties, service fees, and server support payments to the foreign parent at non-arm's length rates to erode the Korean tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income under Article 12 of the International Tax Adjustment Act; additional tax of 10% of the adjusted understated income (up to 20% for fraudulent or grossly negligent noncompliance), plus penalties for failure to file the international related-party transaction statement and documentation (which can be assessed separately under the Act and are nondeductible for corporate income tax).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for transfer pricing adjustments, but the tax authority may pierce the veil when intercompany transactions are transacted fraudulently or have no commercial substance. In such cases directors may be liable for civil damages and jointly liable for the tax and surcharges; persistent deliberate noncompliance can lead to criminal indictment, travel bans, and blacklisting as a serious tax delinquent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Abuse, and Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a mailbox or booking entity that merely holds anti-cheat engine contracts and invoices foreign gaming customers, while all development and decision-making remain outside Korea, and using the Korean corporate identity to obtain Korean treaty benefits, tax subsidies, or dividends without performing any substantial economic activity in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Korean general anti-abuse rule (Framework Act for National Taxes) and the beneficial ownership / limitation-on-benefits provisions of the relevant tax treaty to deny treaty reduction or exemption; re-characterization of transactions, disallowance of deductions, and an additional 30% or more of the tax avoided may be imposed. If the shell is used to move illegal proceeds, the AML regulatory fine can reach KRW 100 million and tax fraud penalties may be added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the shell is a mere conduit; directors may be personally ordered to restore assets and pay avoided tax, subject to asset attachment and departure bans. Criminal exposure extends to fraud, breach of fiduciary duty under the Korean Commercial Act, and anti-money laundering violations, with imprisonment terms up to 5 years when the shell is used for significant tax fraud or financial crime.
